steps_items.heading: Confirm Your Eligibility
steps_items.text: PMI requires a combination of formal education and documented project-management experience. Review PMI's specific requirements for your educational background and years of hands-on project leadership. Granite PM Academy's enrollment team can help you verify eligibility before you enroll.

steps_items.heading: Complete 35 Contact Hours of Training
steps_items.text: Enroll in Granite PM Academy's live-virtual, instructor-led PMP course. Attend interactive sessions led by active certified practitioners covering all five process groups and ten knowledge areas. You'll earn your required contact hours while learning directly from experienced project leaders in a structured classroom environment.

steps_items.heading: Submit Your PMI Application
steps_items.text: After completing your 35 contact hours, submit your formal PMP application to PMI and pay the associated exam fee. Granite PM Academy provides guidance on the application process so your submission meets all PMI requirements. Allow time for PMI to review and approve your candidacy.

steps_items.heading: Prepare and Take the Exam
steps_items.text: Use Granite PM Academy's exam-preparation resources—practice exams, study guides, and instructor support—to build confidence. Schedule your computer-based exam through PMI's testing partner. Your preparation materials align with the current exam blueprint to maximize your readiness.

steps_items.heading: Maintain Your PMP Credential
steps_items.text: After certification, earn Professional Development Units (PDUs) over PMI's standard 3-year renewal cycle to keep your credential active. Granite PM Academy offers PDU-eligible courses and learning opportunities to support your ongoing professional development and career growth.

fq_items.question: What are the PMP eligibility requirements?
fq_items.answer: PMI sets four eligibility paths based on education: a secondary diploma (high school or equivalent) requires 60 months of project leadership experience; an associate's degree requires 48 months; a bachelor's degree requires 36 months; and a bachelor's or postgraduate degree from a PMI Global Accreditation Center (GAC)-accredited program requires just 24 months. Every path also requires 35 hours of project management education — our course satisfies this requirement in full.

fq_items.question: How long does it take to get PMP certified in {city}?
fq_items.answer: After completing training, PMI typically approves applications within 5–10 business days. Once approved, you have one year to sit for the exam. Most students study 4–8 weeks after the course before scheduling their exam.

fq_items.question: What is your pass guarantee?
fq_items.answer: If you complete our course and do not pass the PMP exam within 90 days, we provide additional coaching sessions at no additional cost until you pass.

fq_items.question: Is this training PMI-approved?
fq_items.answer: Yes. Granite PM Academy is a PMI Premier Authorized Training Partner (ATP). Our curriculum is aligned to PMI’s current Examination Content Outline and our contact hours are fully accepted by PMI.

fq_items.question: Is PMP certification worth it for Seattle tech and retail project managers?
fq_items.answer: Seattle's concentration of large employers—Amazon, Starbucks, Expedia Group, and Zillow among them—regularly manage complex, multi-year programs where PMP® certification is valued as proof of structured methodology. While general project manager salaries in Seattle range roughly $112,000–$117,000 annually, PMI® research shows certified practitioners report a median salary premium of approximately $26,000 over non-certified peers nationally, a gap that typically holds across major markets. The credential is most relevant if your role involves cross-functional teams, budgeting, or long-cycle delivery.

fq_items.answer: Technology, retail, travel and logistics, healthcare, and higher education dominate Seattle's employment landscape, and all rely on PMP®-certified practitioners for infrastructure projects and product delivery. If you work in any of these sectors locally, certification typically signals competency to hiring managers and supports advancement into senior delivery roles.

fq_items.question: Should Seattle project managers pursue PMP certification before or during a job search?
fq_items.answer: Timing depends on your current role stability and market readiness. If you are employed and seeking promotion or a strategic move within Seattle's competitive tech and healthcare sectors, earning PMP® certification while working strengthens your candidacy. If you are between roles, completing certification first can accelerate interviews and hiring conversations, especially in industries like logistics and manufacturing where credential demand is high. Either path is viable; the key is committing to preparation aligned with your career timeline.
